title.zh: 卷一百三十九 列傳第二十六: 乃蠻台 朵兒只 朵爾直班 阿魯圖 紐的該
title.en: Volume 139 Biographies 26: Naimantai, Duo'erzhi, Duo'erzhiban, Alutu, Niudegai
title.raw: 卷一百三十九 列傳第二十六: 乃蠻台 朵兒只 朵爾直班 阿魯圖 紐的該 Volume 139 Biographies 26: Naimantai, Duo'erzhi, Duo'erzhiban, Alutu, Niudegai

sentences.zh: 乃蛮台

translations.literal: Naimantai
translations.idiomatic: Naimantai

sentences.zh: 乃蛮台，木华黎五世孙。

translations.literal: Naimantai was a fifth-generation descendant of Muqali.
translations.idiomatic: Naimantai was a fifth-generation descendant of Muqali.

sentences.zh: 曾祖曰孛鲁；

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was named Boru.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was named Boru.

sentences.zh: 祖曰阿礼吉失，追封莒王，谥忠惠；

translations.literal: His grandfather was Alajishi, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Ju with the canon name Zhonghui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Alajishi was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Ju with the posthumous name Zhonghui.

sentences.zh: 父曰忽速忽尔，嗣国王，追封蓟王。

translations.literal: His father was Husuhuer, who succeeded to the kingship and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His father Husuhuer succeeded to the kingship and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Ji.

sentences.zh: 乃蛮台身长七尺，挚静有威，性明果善断，射能贯札。

translations.literal: Naimantai stood seven feet tall, was steady and reserved yet commanding in bearing, clear-minded and decisive by nature, and in archery could pierce a target board.
translations.idiomatic: Naimantai stood seven feet tall. Steady and reserved, he had a commanding presence; he was clear-minded and decisive, and in archery could pierce a target board.

sentences.zh: 大德五年，奉命征海都、朵哇，以功赐貂裘白金，授宣徽院使，阶荣禄大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dade, he was ordered to campaign against Kaidu and Duwa; for his merit he was granted a sable coat and white silver, appointed superintendent of the Imperial Household Directorate, and given the rank of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dade he was ordered to campaign against Kaidu and Duwa. For his service he received a sable coat and white silver, was appointed superintendent of the Imperial Household Directorate, and was given the rank of grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 七年，拜岭北行省右丞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief of the Lingbei Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief of the Lingbei Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 旧制，募民中粮以饷边，是岁中者三十万石。

translations.literal: Under the old regulations, commoners were recruited to deliver grain to the interior as rations for the frontier; that year thirty thousand piculs were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations commoners were recruited to deliver grain inland to supply the frontier; that year thirty thousand piculs qualified.

sentences.zh: 用事者挟私为市，杀其数为十万，民进退失措。

translations.literal: Men in power pursued private gain in the market, cut the figure to one hundred thousand, and the people were at a loss whether to advance or withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power pursued private deals and cut the quota to one hundred thousand piculs, leaving the people unsure whether to go forward or back.

sentences.zh: 乃蛮台请于朝，凡所输者悉受之，以为下年之数，民感其德。

translations.literal: Naimantai requested of the court that all grain delivered be accepted and counted toward the following year's quota; the people were moved by his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Naimantai asked the court to accept every picul delivered and credit it to the next year's quota, and the people were grateful for his kindness.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，改甘肃行省平章政事，佩金虎符。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi he was transferred to be pacification commissioner of the Gansu Branch Secretariat and wore the golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhizhi he was made pacification commissioner of the Gansu Branch Secretariat and wore the golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 甘肃岁籴粮于兰州，多至二万石，距宁夏各千餘里至甘州，自甘州又千餘里始达亦集乃路，而宁夏距亦集乃仅千里。

translations.literal: Gansu each year purchased grain at Lanzhou, often up to twenty thousand piculs; from Ningxia it was more than a thousand li to Ganzhou, and from Ganzhou another thousand li before one reached the Yijinai Circuit, whereas Ningxia was only a thousand li from Yijinai.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Gansu purchased grain at Lanzhou, often as much as twenty thousand piculs. From Ningxia it was more than a thousand li to Ganzhou, and from Ganzhou another thousand li before one reached the Yijinai circuit, while Ningxia was only a thousand li from Yijinai.

sentences.zh: 乃蛮台下谕令挽者自宁夏径趋亦集乃，岁省费六十万缗。

translations.literal: Naimantai issued orders that the haulers should go straight from Ningxia to Yijinai, saving six hundred thousand strings in expenses for the year.
translations.idiomatic: Naimantai ordered the haulers to go straight from Ningxia to Yijinai, saving six hundred thousand strings in expenses that year.

sentences.zh: 天历二年，迁陕西行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianli he was transferred to be pacification commissioner of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianli he was transferred to pacification commissioner of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 关中大饥，诏募民入粟予爵。

translations.literal: Within the passes there was great famine; an edict recruited commoners to submit grain in exchange for ennoblement.
translations.idiomatic: The Guanzhong region suffered severe famine, and an edict recruited commoners to submit grain in exchange for ennoblement.

sentences.zh: 四方富民应命输粟，露积关下。

translations.literal: Wealthy men from all quarters answered the summons and delivered grain, which lay piled in the open below the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy men from all quarters answered the summons and delivered grain, which lay piled in the open below the passes.

sentences.zh: 初，河南饥，告籴关中，而关中民遏其籴。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Henan was in famine, it requested to purchase grain within the passes, but the people within the passes obstructed the sale.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Henan was starving, it asked to buy grain within the passes, but the local people blocked the sales.

sentences.zh: 至是关吏乃河南人，修宿怨，拒粟使不得入。

translations.literal: Now the pass officials were men from Henan; nursing old grievances, they refused the grain envoys entry.
translations.idiomatic: By then the pass officials were men from Henan. Nursing old grievances, they refused to let the grain envoys enter.

sentences.zh: 乃蛮台杖关吏而入其粟。

translations.literal: Naimantai had the pass officials beaten and admitted the grain.
translations.idiomatic: Naimantai had the pass officials beaten and let the grain in.

sentences.zh: 京兆民掠人而食之，则命分健卒为队，捕强食人者，其患乃已。

translations.literal: In Jingzhao the people plundered others and ate human flesh; he then ordered strong soldiers divided into squads to capture those who forcibly ate people, and the scourge ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingzhao people were robbing and eating one another. He ordered picked troops divided into squads to capture those who forcibly ate human flesh, and the scourge ceased.

sentences.zh: 时入关粟虽多，而贫民乏钞以籴。

translations.literal: At the time grain entering the passes was plentiful, yet the poor lacked paper money to buy it.
translations.idiomatic: Although grain entering the passes was plentiful, the poor lacked banknotes to buy it.

sentences.zh: 乃蛮台取官库未毁昏钞，得五百万缗，识以省印，给民行用，俟官给赈饥钞，如数易之。

translations.literal: Naimantai took worn notes from the government treasury that had not yet been destroyed, obtaining five million strings; he marked them with the provincial seal, issued them for the people to use, and when the court later issued famine-relief notes, exchanged them one for one.
translations.idiomatic: Naimantai took worn notes from the government treasury that had not yet been destroyed, obtaining five million strings. He stamped them with the provincial seal and put them into circulation; when the court later issued famine-relief notes, he exchanged them at full value.

sentences.zh: 先时，民或就食他所，多毁墙屋以往。

translations.literal: Previously, when people went elsewhere to seek food, many tore down their walls and houses to take with them.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when people went elsewhere to seek food, many tore down their walls and houses to take with them.

sentences.zh: 乃蛮台谕之曰：「明年岁稔，尔当复还，其勿毁之。」

translations.literal: Naimantai instructed them, saying: "Next year the harvest will be good; you should return, and you must not destroy them."
translations.idiomatic: Naimantai told them, "Next year the harvest will be good and you will return. Do not destroy your homes."

sentences.zh: 民由是不敢毁，及明年还，皆得按堵如初。

translations.literal: The people therefore did not dare destroy them, and when they returned the next year all were able to settle in peace as before.
translations.idiomatic: The people therefore did not dare destroy them, and when they returned the next year all were able to settle in peace as before.

sentences.zh: 拜西行台御史大夫，赐金币、玩服等物。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand censor of the Western Branch Secretariat and was granted gold coins, curios, robes, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand censor of the Western Branch Secretariat and was granted gold coins, curios, robes, and the like.

sentences.zh: 奉命送太宗皇帝旧铸皇兄之宝于其后嗣燕只哥䚟，乃蛮台威望素严，至其境，礼貌益尊。

translations.literal: Ordered to deliver the Taizong Emperor's old-cast treasure of the imperial elder brother to his descendant Yanzhige, Naimantai's prestige had always been severe; upon reaching that territory, the courtesy shown him grew still more respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to deliver the Taizong Emperor's old-cast treasure of the imperial elder brother to his descendant Yanzhige. Naimantai's prestige had always been formidable, and upon reaching that territory the courtesy shown him grew still more respectful.

sentences.zh: 至顺元年，迁上都留守，佩元降虎符，虎贲亲军都指挥使，进阶开府仪同三司，知岭北行枢密院事，封宣宁郡王，赐金印。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun he was transferred to be intendant of the Upper Capital, wore the tiger tally of the Yuan descent, became commander-in-chief of the Tiger-Gallant Personal Army, was advanced to the rank of Grand Preceptor with the Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes, directed the affairs of the Lingbei Branch Privy Council, was enfeoffed as Prince of the Commandery of Xuanding, and was granted a golden seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhishun he was transferred to intendant of the Upper Capital, wore the tiger tally of the Yuan descent, became commander-in-chief of the Tiger-Gallant personal army, was advanced to grand preceptor with protocol equal to the three dukes, directed the Lingbei Branch Privy Council, was enfeoffed as prince of Xuanding commandery, and was granted a golden seal.

sentences.zh: 寻奉命出镇北边，锡予尤重。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to go out and guard the northern frontier, and the gifts bestowed were especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was ordered to guard the northern frontier, and the gifts bestowed were especially generous.

sentences.zh: 国初，诸军置万户、千户、百户，时金银符未备，惟加缨于枪以为等威。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state, the armies were organized with commanders of ten thousand, one thousand, and one hundred; at the time gold and silver tallies were not yet ready, and tassels were added to spears alone to mark rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the state the armies had commanders of ten thousand, one thousand, and one hundred; gold and silver tallies were not yet ready, and tassels were added to spears alone to mark rank.

sentences.zh: 至是乃蛮台为请于朝，皆得绾符。

translations.literal: Now Naimantai requested this of the court, and all received official tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Now Naimantai requested this of the court, and all received official tallies.

sentences.zh: 后至元三年，诏乃蛮台袭国王，授以金印。

translations.literal: In the third year of Houzhiyuan an edict ordered Naimantai to succeed to the kingship and granted him a golden seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Houzhiyuan an edict ordered Naimantai to succeed to the kingship and granted him a golden seal.

sentences.zh: 继又以安边睦邻之功，赐珠络半臂并海东名鹰、西域文豹，国制以此为极恩。

translations.literal: Later, for merit in securing the frontier and keeping peace with neighbors, he was granted a pearl-net half-sleeve together with a famous hawk from the Eastern Sea and a patterned leopard from the Western Regions; under the national regulations this was regarded as the utmost favor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for securing the frontier and keeping peace with neighbors, he was granted a pearl-net half-sleeve together with a famous hawk from the Eastern Sea and a patterned leopard from the Western Regions—under national custom the highest favor.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜岭北行省左丞相，仍前国王、知行枢密院事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed left chief councilor of the Lingbei Branch Secretariat, retaining his former kingship and concurrently directing the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed left chief councilor of the Lingbei Branch Secretariat, retaining his kingship and concurrently directing the privy council.

sentences.zh: 至正二年，迁辽阳行省左丞相，以年逾六十，上疏辞职归。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizheng he was transferred to left chief councilor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat; as he was over sixty, he memorialized to resign and return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhizheng he was transferred to left chief councilor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat. Over sixty, he memorialized to resign and return home.

sentences.zh: 念其军士贫乏，以麦四百石、马二百匹、羊五百头遍给之。

translations.literal: Mindful that his soldiers were poor, he distributed four hundred piculs of wheat, two hundred horses, and five hundred sheep among them throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that his soldiers were poor, he distributed four hundred piculs of wheat, two hundred horses, and five hundred sheep among them.

sentences.zh: 八年，薨于家，帝闻之震悼，命有司厚致赙仪，诏赠摅忠宣惠绥远辅治功臣、太师、开府仪同三司、上柱国，追封鲁王，谥忠穆。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died at home; when the emperor heard of it he was deeply shaken and grieved, ordered the relevant offices to provide generous funeral gifts, and by edict posthumously granted him the title of Meritous Minister Who Displays Loyalty, Proclaims Kindness, Pacifies the Distant, and Assists in Governance, Grand Preceptor, Grand Preceptor with the Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes, and Supreme Pillar of the State, enfeoffing him posthumously as Prince of Lu with the posthumous name Zhongmu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died at home. The emperor was deeply shaken and grieved, ordered the relevant offices to provide generous funeral gifts, and by edict posthumously granted him meritous minister who displays loyalty, proclaims kindness, pacifies the distant, and assists in governance, grand preceptor, grand preceptor with protocol equal to the three dukes, and supreme pillar of the state, enfeoffing him posthumously as Prince of Lu with the posthumous name Zhongmu.

sentences.zh: 子二：长野仙溥化，入宿卫，掌速古兒赤，特授朝列大夫、给事中，拜监察御史，继除河西廉访副使、淮西宣慰副使，累迁中书参知政事，由御史中丞为中书右丞；

translations.literal: He had two sons: the elder Yexianpuhua entered the palace guard, held the office of suguerchi, was specially appointed Court Gentleman for Cherished Conduct and Attendant of the Secretariat, was made investigating censor, then successively removed to be associate surveillance commissioner of Hexi and associate pacification commissioner of Huaixi, and was repeatedly promoted to associate administrative councilor of the Secretariat, rising from vice censor-in-chief to right chief councilor of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons. The elder, Yexianpuhua, entered the palace guard and held the office of suguerchi. He was specially appointed court gentleman for cherished conduct and attendant of the secretariat, made investigating censor, then successively associate surveillance commissioner of Hexi and associate pacification commissioner of Huaixi, and was repeatedly promoted to associate administrative councilor of the Secretariat, rising from vice censor-in-chief to right chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 次晃忽而不花。

translations.literal: the younger Huanghuerbuhua.
translations.idiomatic: The younger was Huanghuerbuhua.

sentences.zh: 朵兒只

translations.literal: Duo'erzhi
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhi

sentences.zh: 朵兒只，木华黎六世孙，脱脱子也。

translations.literal: Duo'erzhi was a sixth-generation descendant of Muqali and the son of Toghto.
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhi was a sixth-generation descendant of Muqali and the son of Toghto.

sentences.zh: 朵兒只生一岁而孤，稍长，备宿卫，事母至孝，喜读书，不屑屑事章句，于古君臣行事忠君爱民之道，多所究心。

translations.literal: Duo'erzhi lost his father when one year old; when he grew somewhat older he served in the palace guard, was filial toward his mother to the utmost, loved reading, and disdained to fuss over textual glosses, yet devoted much study to the ways of ancient ruler and minister in loyalty to the sovereign and love for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhi lost his father at the age of one. When he grew older he served in the palace guard, was devoted to his mother, loved reading, and disdained textual glosses, yet studied deeply how ancient rulers and ministers were loyal to the sovereign and cared for the people.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，授中奉大夫、集贤学士，时年未及冠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi he was appointed Grand Master for Cherished Conduct and academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, though he had not yet reached the capping age.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhizhi he was appointed grand master for cherished conduct and academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, though he had not yet reached the capping age.

sentences.zh: 一时同寅如郭贯、赵世延、邓文原诸老皆器重之。

translations.literal: At the time his colleagues such as the elders Guo Guan, Zhao Shiyan, and Deng Wenyuan all held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his colleagues among the senior men—Guo Guan, Zhao Shiyan, and Deng Wenyuan—all held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 天历元年，朵罗台国王自上都领兵至古北口，与大都兵迎敌。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli, King Duoluotai led troops from the Upper Capital to Gubeikou to meet the army of Dadu in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianli King Duoluotai led troops from the Upper Capital to Gubeikou to meet the army of Dadu in battle.

sentences.zh: 事定，文宗杀朵罗台。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Emperor Wenzong executed Duoluotai.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, Emperor Wenzong executed Duoluotai.

sentences.zh: 二年，朵兒只袭国王位，扈跸上都，诏便道至辽阳之国。

translations.literal: In the second year Duo'erzhi succeeded to the kingship, accompanied the imperial procession to the Upper Capital, and was ordered by edict to proceed by convenient route to his domain in Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Duo'erzhi succeeded to the kingship, accompanied the imperial procession to the Upper Capital, and was ordered by edict to proceed by convenient route to his domain in Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 顺帝至元四年，朵罗台弟乃蛮台恃太师伯颜势，谓国王位乃其所当袭，诉于朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan under Emperor Shundi, Duoluotai's younger brother Naimantai, relying on the power of Grand Preceptor Bayan, said the kingship was what he ought to inherit and appealed to the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan under Emperor Shundi, Duoluotai's younger brother Naimantai, relying on Grand Preceptor Bayan's power, said the kingship was rightfully his and appealed to the court.

sentences.zh: 伯颜妻欲得朵兒只大珠环，价直万六千锭。

translations.literal: Bayan's wife wanted Duo'erzhi's great pearl ring, worth sixteen thousand ingots.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan's wife wanted Duo'erzhi's great pearl ring, worth sixteen thousand ingots.

sentences.zh: 朵兒只无以应，则慨然曰：「王位我祖宗所传，不宜从人求买。

translations.literal: Duo'erzhi had nothing with which to respond and said with indignation: "The kingship was transmitted by my ancestors; one ought not to seek to buy it from others.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to comply, Duo'erzhi said indignantly, "The kingship was transmitted by my ancestors. One ought not to buy it from others.

sentences.zh: 我纵不得为，设为之，亦我宗族人耳。」

translations.literal: Even if I cannot obtain it, if it is done, it will still be a man of my clan."
translations.idiomatic: Even if I cannot keep it, whoever receives it will still be a man of my clan."

sentences.zh: 于是乃蛮台以赂故得为国王，而除朵兒只辽阳行省左丞相。

translations.literal: Thereupon Naimantai obtained the kingship because of bribes, while Duo'erzhi was appointed left chief councilor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Naimantai obtained the kingship through bribery, while Duo'erzhi was appointed left chief councilor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以安靖为治，民用不扰。

translations.literal: He governed with tranquillity as his aim, and the people's livelihood was undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with tranquillity as his aim, and the people's livelihood was undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 六年，迁河南行省左丞相，为政如在辽阳时。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to left chief councilor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, governing as he had in Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to left chief councilor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, governing as he had in Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，河南范孟为乱，以诖误连系者千百计。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fan Meng rebelled in Henan, those implicated by error and linked together numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Fan Meng rebelled in Henan, those implicated by error and linked together numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 朵兒只至，颇知其冤，力欲直之，而平章政事纳麟乃元问官，执其说不从。

translations.literal: When Duo'erzhi arrived he knew well that they were wronged and strove to set them right, but the pacification commissioner Nalin, who had been the Yuan interrogation official, clung to his view and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo'erzhi arrived he knew they were wronged and strove to clear them, but pacification commissioner Nalin, who had been the Yuan interrogation official, clung to his view and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 已而纳麟还，言于朝，以谓朵兒只心徇汉人。

translations.literal: Before long Nalin returned and spoke to the court, saying that Duo'erzhi's heart favored the Han people.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Nalin returned to court and said Duo'erzhi favored the Han people.

sentences.zh: 朵兒只为人宽弘有度，亦不恤也。

translations.literal: Duo'erzhi was broad-minded and measured in character and did not concern himself with it.
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhi was broad-minded and measured in character and paid it no heed.

sentences.zh: 至正四年，迁江浙行省左丞相。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhizheng he was transferred to left chief councilor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhizheng he was transferred to left chief councilor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 时杭城荐经灾毁，别兒怯不花先为相，庶务宽纾，朵兒只继之，咸仍其旧，民心翕然。

translations.literal: At the time Hangzhou had repeatedly suffered disaster and ruin; Bieqiebuha had first served as chief minister and had eased the multitude of affairs; Duo'erzhi succeeded him and all continued as before, and the people's hearts were united.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou had repeatedly suffered disaster and ruin. Bieqiebuha had first served as chief minister and eased the multitude of affairs; Duo'erzhi succeeded him and continued as before, and the people's hearts were united.

sentences.zh: 汀州寇窃发，朵兒只调遣将士招捕之，威信所及，数月即平。

translations.literal: Bandits stole out in Tingzhou; Duo'erzhi dispatched officers and soldiers to recruit and capture them, and where his authority and trust reached, within a few months they were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits broke out in Tingzhou. Duo'erzhi dispatched officers and soldiers to recruit and capture them, and where his authority and trust reached, within a few months order was restored.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其绩，锡九龙衣、上尊酒。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his achievement and granted him the nine-dragon robe and superior wine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his achievement and granted him the nine-dragon robe and superior wine.

sentences.zh: 居二年，方面晏然。

translations.literal: After two years the region was entirely calm.
translations.idiomatic: After two years the region was entirely calm.

sentences.zh: 杭之耆老請建生祠，如前丞相故事，朵兒只辭之曰：「昔者我父平章官浙省，我實生於此，宜爾父老有愛於我，我於爾杭人得無情乎？

translations.literal: The elders of Hangzhou requested permission to build a living shrine for him, following the precedent of a former chief minister, but Duo'erzhi declined, saying: "Formerly my father held a chief-councilor post in Zhejiang Province, and I was in fact born here; it is fitting that you elders have affection for me, and how could I be without feeling for you people of Hangzhou?
translations.idiomatic: The elders of Hangzhou asked to build a living shrine for him, following the precedent of a former chief minister, but Duo'erzhi declined: "Formerly my father held a chief-councilor post in Zhejiang Province, and I was born here, so it is natural that you elders care for me. How could I have no feeling for the people of Hangzhou?

sentences.zh: 然今天下承平，我叨居相位於此，唯知謹守法度不辱先人足矣，何用虛名為？」

translations.literal: Yet today the realm is at peace; I am honored to hold the chancellorship here and need only carefully keep the laws and not disgrace my forebears--that is enough. What use is an empty name?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet today the realm is at peace. I am honored to hold the chancellorship here and need only keep the laws carefully and avoid disgracing my forebears; that is enough. What use is an empty name?"

sentences.zh: 七年，召拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned and appointed grand censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was summoned and appointed grand censor.

sentences.zh: 会丞相虚位，秋，拜中书左丞相。

translations.literal: As the chancellorship was vacant, in autumn he was appointed left chief councilor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: As the chancellorship was vacant, in autumn he was appointed left chief councilor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 冬，升右丞相、监修国史，而太平为左丞相。

translations.literal: In winter he was promoted to right chief councilor and supervisor of the compilation of the national history, while Taiping served as left chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he was promoted to right chief councilor and supervisor of the compilation of the national history, while Taiping served as left chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 是时，朝廷无事，稽古礼文之事，有坠必举，请赐经筵讲官坐，以崇圣学，选清望官专典陈言，以求治道，核守令六事，沙汰僧尼，举隐逸士，事见《太平传》。

translations.literal: At that time the court had no pressing affairs; in matters of examining antiquity and ritual texts, whatever had fallen away was revived. He requested seats for the lecturers at the Classics Colloquium to honor sagely learning, selected officials of clear reputation to specialize in presenting remonstrances to seek the way of governance, examined the six duties of prefects and magistrates, sifted Buddhist monks and nuns, and recommended reclusive scholars—these matters are recorded in the 《Biography of Taiping》.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court had no pressing affairs. Whatever ritual and classical matters had fallen away were revived. He requested seats for the Classics Colloquium lecturers to honor sagely learning, selected officials of clear reputation to present remonstrances and seek the way of governance, examined the six duties of prefects and magistrates, sifted Buddhist monks and nuns, and recommended reclusive scholars—these matters are recorded in the 《Biography of Taiping》.

sentences.zh: 岁余，留守司行致贺礼，其物先留鸿禧观，将馈二相。

translations.literal: After more than a year the Intendant's Office of the Upper Capital performed congratulatory rites; the goods were first left at the Hongxi Abbey, to be presented to the two chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year the Upper Capital intendant's office performed congratulatory rites. The goods were first left at Hongxi Abbey to be presented to the two chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 朵兒只家臣寓观中，察知物有丰杀，其致左相者特丰。

translations.literal: Duo'erzhi's household staff lodged in the abbey and observed that the goods varied in abundance; those for the left chief minister were especially plentiful.
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhi's household staff lodged in the abbey and observed that the gifts varied in abundance; those for the left chief minister were especially plentiful.

sentences.zh: 家臣具白其事，请却之。

translations.literal: The household staff fully reported the matter and asked to refuse them.
translations.idiomatic: The household staff reported the matter in full and asked to refuse the gifts.

sentences.zh: 朵兒只曰：「彼纵不送我，亦又何怪。」

translations.literal: Duo'erzhi said: "Even if they do not send them to me, what is there to wonder at?"
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhi said, "Even if they send nothing to me, what is there to wonder at?"

sentences.zh: 即命受之。

translations.literal: He at once ordered them accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He at once ordered them accepted.

sentences.zh: 郯王家产既籍于官，朵兒只俾掾史录其数。

translations.literal: The Prince of Tan's household property had already been registered with the government; Duo'erzhi had a clerk record the tally.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Tan's household property had already been registered with the government. Duo'erzhi had a clerk record the tally.

sentences.zh: 明日，掾史以复。

translations.literal: The next day the clerk reported back.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the clerk reported back.

sentences.zh: 韩嘉讷为平章，不知出丞相命，勃然变色，叱掾史曰：「公事须自下而上，何竟白丞相！」

translations.literal: Han Jiane was pacification commissioner and, not knowing it was by the chief minister's order, flushed with anger and rebuked the clerk: "Public business must go from below to above—why report straight to the chief minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiane was pacification commissioner. Not knowing it was by the chief minister's order, he flushed with anger and rebuked the clerk, "Public business must go from below to above—why report straight to the chief minister!"

sentences.zh: 令客省使扶出。

translations.literal: He ordered the guest-reception commissioner to escort him out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the guest-reception commissioner to escort him out.

sentences.zh: 朵兒只不为动，知者咸服其量。

translations.literal: Duo'erzhi was unmoved; those who knew the matter all admired his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhi was unmoved; those who knew the matter all admired his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 九年，罢丞相位，复为国王，之国辽阳。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was dismissed from the chancellorship, again became king, and went to his domain in Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was dismissed from the chancellorship, again became king, and went to his domain in Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 十四年，诏脱脱总兵南讨。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an edict ordered Toghto to command troops in a southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year an edict ordered Toghto to command troops in a southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 中书参议龚伯遂建言：「宜分遣诸宗王及异姓王俱出军。」

translations.literal: Associate deliberator of the Secretariat Gong Boshui proposed: "The various imperial princes and non-imperial princes should all be sent out with troops separately."
translations.idiomatic: Associate deliberator of the Secretariat Gong Boshui proposed, "The various imperial princes and non-imperial princes should all be sent out with troops separately."

sentences.zh: 吴王朵尔赤厚赂伯遂获免。

translations.literal: Prince Wu Duoerchi bribed Boshui heavily and was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wu Duoerchi bribed Boshui heavily and was exempted.

sentences.zh: 朵兒只独曰：「吾国家世臣，天下有事，政效力之秋也，吾岂暇与小子辈通贿赂哉！」

translations.literal: Duo'erzhi alone said: "Our family has been hereditary ministers for generations; when the realm has business, this is the season to exert our strength—how could I have leisure to traffic in bribes with petty fellows!"
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhi alone said, "Our family has been hereditary ministers for generations. When the realm has need, this is the season to exert our strength—how could I traffic in bribes with petty fellows!"

sentences.zh: 即领兵出淮南，听脱脱节制。

translations.literal: He at once led troops into Huainan and obeyed Toghto's command.
translations.idiomatic: He at once led troops into Huainan and obeyed Toghto's command.

sentences.zh: 脱脱遣朵兒只攻六合，拔之。

translations.literal: Toghto dispatched Duo'erzhi to attack Liuhe, and he captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Toghto dispatched Duo'erzhi to attack Liuhe, and he captured it.

sentences.zh: 既而诏削脱脱官爵，罢其兵权，朵兒只乃以本部兵守扬州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward an edict stripped Toghto of office and rank and removed his military authority; Duo'erzhi then guarded Yangzhou with his own troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an edict stripped Toghto of office and rank and removed his military authority. Duo'erzhi then guarded Yangzhou with his own troops.

sentences.zh: 十五年，薨于军，年五十二。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died in the army at the age of fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he died in the army at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 初，朵兒只为集贤学士，从其从兄丞相拜住在上都。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Duo'erzhi was academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, he followed his cousin by the mother's side, Chief Councilor Baizhu, at the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Duo'erzhi was academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, he followed his cousin by the mother's side, Chief Councilor Baizhu, at the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 南坡之变，拜住遇害。

translations.literal: In the Nampa Incident, Baizhu met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the Nampa Incident Baizhu was killed.

sentences.zh: 贼臣铁失、赤斤铁木兒等并欲杀朵兒只，其从子朵尔直班方八岁，走诣怯薛官失都兒求免，以故朵兒只得脱于难。

translations.literal: The traitorous ministers Tieshi, Chijintiemuer, and the rest all wished to kill Duo'erzhi as well; his nephew Duo'erzhiban was then eight years old, ran to the kheshig officer Shiduer to beg for mercy, and for this reason Duo'erzhi escaped the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The traitorous ministers Tieshi, Chijintiemuer, and the rest all wished to kill Duo'erzhi as well. His nephew Duo'erzhiban was then eight years old, ran to the kheshig officer Shiduer to beg for mercy, and for this reason Duo'erzhi escaped the calamity.

sentences.zh: 朵兒只为相，务存大体，而太平则兼理庶务，一时政权颇出于太平，趋附者众，朵兒只处之凝然，不与较。

translations.literal: When Duo'erzhi was chief minister he strove to preserve the larger pattern, while Taiping also handled the multitude of affairs; for a time political power leaned largely toward Taiping, and many rushed to attach themselves to him; Duo'erzhi remained composed and did not contend.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister Duo'erzhi strove to preserve the larger pattern, while Taiping also handled the multitude of affairs. For a time political power leaned largely toward Taiping and many rushed to attach themselves to him, yet Duo'erzhi remained composed and did not contend.

sentences.zh: 然太平亦能推让尽礼，中外皆号为贤相云。

translations.literal: Yet Taiping also could yield and show full courtesy; within and without the court all called them worthy chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Taiping also could yield and show full courtesy; within and without the court all called them worthy chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 二子：朵蛮帖木兒，翰林学士；

translations.literal: He had two sons: Duomantiemuer, Hanlin academician;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Duomantiemuer, a Hanlin academician;

sentences.zh: 俺木哥失里，袭国王。

translations.literal: Anmugeshili, who succeeded to the kingship.
translations.idiomatic: and Anmugeshili, who succeeded to the kingship.

sentences.zh: 朵尔直班

translations.literal: Duo'erzhiban
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhiban

sentences.zh: 朵尔直班，字惟中，木华黎七世孙。

translations.literal: Duo'erzhiban, style name Weizhong, was a seventh-generation descendant of Muqali.
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhiban, style name Weizhong, was a seventh-generation descendant of Muqali.

sentences.zh: 祖曰硕德，父曰别理哥帖木尔。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Shude; his father was Bieligetiemu'er.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Shude; his father was Bieligetiemu'er.

sentences.zh: 朵尔直班甫晬而孤，育于从祖母。

translations.literal: Duo'erzhiban lost his father when still in swaddling clothes and was raised by his father's cousin's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhiban lost his father while still in swaddling clothes and was raised by his father's cousin's wife.

sentences.zh: 拜住，从父也，请于仁宗，降玺书护其家。

translations.literal: Baizhu, his cousin by the mother's side, requested of Emperor Renzong, who lowered an imperial letter to protect his household.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu, his cousin by the mother's side, asked Emperor Renzong for an imperial letter to protect his household.

sentences.zh: 稍长，好读书。

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older, he loved reading.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew older he loved reading.

sentences.zh: 年十四，见文宗，适将幸上都，亲阅御衣，命录于簿，顾左右无能书汉字者，朵尔直班引笔书之。

translations.literal: At fourteen he was received by Emperor Wenzong; as the emperor was about to proceed to the Upper Capital, he personally inspected the imperial robes and ordered them recorded in the register. Seeing that none among those at hand could write Chinese characters, Duo'erzhiban took up the brush and wrote them.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he was received by Emperor Wenzong. As the emperor was about to proceed to the Upper Capital he personally inspected the imperial robes and ordered them recorded; none at hand could write Chinese characters, so Duo'erzhiban took up the brush and wrote them.

sentences.zh: 文宗喜曰：「世臣之家乃能知学，岂易得哉！」

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong said with pleasure: "In a hereditary minister's household one can yet know learning—how could that be easily obtained!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong said with pleasure, "A hereditary minister's household that still values learning—how rare!"

sentences.zh: 命为尚衣奉御，寻授工部郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe, and soon after made director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attendant of the imperial wardrobe and soon made director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 元统元年，擢监察御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuantong he was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 首上疏，请亲祀宗庙，赦命不宜数。

translations.literal: He first submitted a memorial requesting that the emperor personally sacrifice at the ancestral temple and that amnesties should not be issued too frequently.
translations.idiomatic: In his first memorial he asked the emperor to sacrifice personally at the ancestral temple and urged that amnesties not be issued too frequently.

sentences.zh: 又陈时政五事，其一曰：「太史言三月癸卯望月食既，四月戊午朔，日又食。

translations.literal: He also presented five matters on current policy. The first said: "The Grand Astrologer reports that on the third month, guimao day, the moon will suffer a total eclipse, and on the fourth month, wuwu day, the first day of the month, the sun will also be eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: He also presented five matters on current policy. The first said, "The grand astrologer reports a total lunar eclipse on the guimao day of the third month and a solar eclipse on the wuwu day, the first of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 皇上宜奋乾纲，修刑政，疏远邪佞，颛任忠良，庶可消弭灾变以为祯祥。」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ought to exert the power of Qian, rectify punishments and government, keep distant evil and flatterers, and devote himself solely to loyal and good men—then perhaps the calamities may be dissolved and turned into auspicious signs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ought to exert the power of Qian, rectify punishments and government, keep distant evil and flatterers, and devote himself solely to loyal and good men, so that calamities may be dissolved and turned into auspicious signs."

sentences.zh: 二曰：「亲祀郊庙。」

translations.literal: The second said: "Personally sacrifice at the suburban altars and ancestral temple."
translations.idiomatic: The second said, "Personally sacrifice at the suburban altars and ancestral temple."

sentences.zh: 三曰：「博选勋旧世臣之子，端谨正直之人，前后辅导，使嬉戏之事不接于目，俚俗之言不及于耳，则圣德日新矣。」

translations.literal: The third said: "Broadly select sons of meritorious old hereditary houses and men who are upright and proper to assist before and after, so that matters of play do not reach the eyes and vulgar speech does not reach the ears—then sagely virtue will renew day by day."
translations.idiomatic: The third said, "Broadly select sons of meritorious old houses and upright men to assist the heir before and after, so that play does not reach his eyes and vulgar speech his ears, and sagely virtue will renew day by day."

sentences.zh: 四曰：「枢机之臣固宜尊宠，然必赏罚公，则民心服。」

translations.literal: The fourth said: "Ministers who hold the keys of power should indeed be honored, yet rewards and punishments must be fair—then the people's hearts will be obedient."
translations.idiomatic: The fourth said, "Ministers who hold the keys of power should indeed be honored, yet rewards and punishments must be fair, and the people's hearts will be obedient."

sentences.zh: 五曰：「弭安盗贼，振救饥民。」

translations.literal: The fifth said: "Pacify and suppress bandits and thieves, and relieve and save starving people."
translations.idiomatic: The fifth said, "Pacify bandits and thieves and relieve starving people."

sentences.zh: 是时日月薄蚀，烈风暴作，河北、山东旱蝗为灾，乃复条陈九事上之，一曰：「比日幸门渐启，刑罚渐差，无功者觊觎希赏，有罪者侥幸求免。

translations.literal: At that time the sun and moon suffered thin eclipses, fierce winds and storms arose, and drought and locusts became disasters in Hebei and Shandong; he again set forth nine matters and submitted them. The first said: "Recently the gate of favor has gradually opened and punishments have gradually slackened; those without merit hope for rewards, and the guilty hope by chance to be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the sun and moon suffered thin eclipses, fierce storms arose, and drought and locusts ravaged Hebei and Shandong. He again set forth nine matters. The first said, "Recently the gate of favor has gradually opened and punishments slackened; those without merit hope for rewards and the guilty hope by chance to be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 恐刑政渐隳，纪纲渐紊，劳臣何以示劝，奸臣无所警惧。」

translations.literal: I fear that criminal government will gradually collapse and the great cord will gradually unravel; how can laboring ministers be shown encouragement, and how can wicked ministers be given nothing to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: I fear criminal government will collapse and the great cord unravel; how can laboring ministers be encouraged, and how can wicked ministers be given nothing to fear?"

sentences.zh: 二曰：「天下之财皆出于民，民竭其力以佐公上，而用犹不足，则嗟怨之气上干阴阳之和，水旱灾变所由生也。

translations.literal: The second said: "All wealth under Heaven comes from the people. The people exhaust their strength to assist the public above, yet use is still insufficient—then the sound of sighing and resentment ascends and disturbs the harmony of yin and yang; flood, drought, and disasters arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: The second said, "All wealth under Heaven comes from the people. They exhaust their strength to assist the state, yet use is still insufficient; sighing and resentment then disturb the harmony of yin and yang, and flood, drought, and disasters arise from this.

sentences.zh: 宜颛命中书省官二员，督责户部详定减省，罢不急之工役，止无名之赏赐。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to appoint solely two officials of the Secretariat to supervise and press the Ministry of Revenue to fix reductions in detail, stop unurgent labor corvée, and halt nameless bestowals."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint solely two Secretariat officials to supervise the Ministry of Revenue in fixing reductions, stop unurgent labor corvée, and halt nameless bestowals."

sentences.zh: 三曰：「禁中常作佛事，权宜停止。」

translations.literal: The third said: "Buddhist services within the palace should for the time be stopped as expedient."
translations.idiomatic: The third said, "Buddhist services within the palace should for the time be stopped as expedient."

sentences.zh: 四曰：「官府日增，选法愈敝，宜省冗员。」

translations.literal: The fourth said: "Government offices increase daily and the selection law grows more corrupt; superfluous posts should be cut."
translations.idiomatic: The fourth said, "Government offices increase daily and the selection law grows more corrupt; superfluous posts should be cut."

sentences.zh: 五曰均公田。

translations.literal: The fifth: equalize public fields.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth: equalize public fields.

sentences.zh: 六曰铸钱币。

translations.literal: The sixth: cast money.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth: cast money.

sentences.zh: 七曰罢山东田赋总管府。

translations.literal: The seventh: abolish the Shandong Field-Tax General Office.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh: abolish the Shandong field-tax general office.

sentences.zh: 八曰蠲河南自实田粮。

translations.literal: The eighth: remit the self-assessed field tax of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth: remit the self-assessed field tax of Henan.

sentences.zh: 九曰禁取姬妾于海外。

translations.literal: The ninth: forbid taking concubines from beyond the seas.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth: forbid taking concubines from beyond the seas.

sentences.zh: 正月元日，朝贺大明殿，朵尔直班当纠正班次，即上言：「百官逾越班制者，当同失仪论，以惩不敬。」

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month, when court congratulation was held in the Great Bright Hall, Duo'erzhiban was to correct the order of ranks and at once submitted: "Officials who overstep rank and regulation should be punished together with those who lose ritual deportment, to warn against disrespect."
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, when court congratulation was held in the Great Bright Hall, Duo'erzhiban was to correct the order of ranks and submitted, "Officials who overstep rank should be punished like those who lose ritual deportment, to warn against disrespect."

sentences.zh: 先是，教坊官位在百官后，御史大夫撒迪传旨俾入正班，朵尔直班执不可。

translations.literal: Earlier, the officials of the Music Bureau stood after the hundred officials. Grand Censor Sadi transmitted an edict ordering them into the regular ranks; Duo'erzhiban held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Music Bureau stood after the hundred officials. Grand Censor Sadi transmitted an edict ordering them into the regular ranks, but Duo'erzhiban refused.

sentences.zh: 撒迪曰：「御史不奉诏耶？」

translations.literal: Sadi said: "Does the censor not obey the edict?"
translations.idiomatic: Sadi said, "Does the censor not obey the edict?"

sentences.zh: 朵尔直班曰：「事不可行，大夫宜覆奏可也。」

translations.literal: Duo'erzhiban said: "The matter cannot be carried out; the grand censor ought to memorialize again for approval."
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhiban said, "The matter cannot be carried out. The grand censor ought to memorialize again for approval."

sentences.zh: 西僧为佛事内廷，醉酒失火，朵尔直班劾其不守戒律，延烧宫殿，震惊九重。

translations.literal: Western monks performed Buddhist services within the court, became drunk, and lost fire; Duo'erzhiban impeached them for not keeping discipline, extending the blaze to burn the palaces and shaking the Ninefold Palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Western monks performed Buddhist services within the court, became drunk, and set a fire. Duo'erzhiban impeached them for not keeping discipline; the blaze burned the palaces and shook the Ninefold Palaces.

sentences.zh: 撒迪传旨免其罪，朵尔直班又执不可，一日间传旨者八，乃已。

translations.literal: Sadi transmitted an edict to exempt them from guilt; Duo'erzhiban again held that it could not be done. Within a single day edicts were transmitted eight times before it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Sadi transmitted an edict to exempt them, but Duo'erzhiban again refused. Within a single day edicts were transmitted eight times before it ceased.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯颜、御史大夫唐其势二家家奴怙势为民害，朵尔直班巡历至漷州，悉捕其人致于法，民大悦。

translations.literal: The household slaves of Chief Councilor Bayan and Grand Censor Tangqishi relied on power to harm the people; when Duo'erzhiban made a circuit to Huo Prefecture, he captured them all and brought them under the law, and the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The household slaves of Chief Councilor Bayan and Grand Censor Tangqishi relied on power to harm the people. When Duo'erzhiban made a circuit to Huo Prefecture he captured them all and brought them under the law, and the people were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 及还，唐其势怒曰：「御史不礼我已甚，辱我家人，我何面目见人耶？」

translations.literal: Upon his return Tangqishi said in anger: "The censor has been extremely disrespectful to me and shamed my household—how can I show my face to others?"
translations.idiomatic: Upon his return Tangqishi said angrily, "The censor has been extremely disrespectful to me and shamed my household—how can I show my face?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「朵尔直班知奉法而已，它不知也。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Duo'erzhiban knows only to uphold the law; he knows nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Duo'erzhiban knows only to uphold the law; he knows nothing else."

sentences.zh: 唐其势从子马马沙为钦察亲军指挥使，恣横不法，朵尔直班劾奏之。

translations.literal: Tangqishi's nephew Mamasha was commander of the Qipchaq Personal Army and acted lawlessly with arrogant license; Duo'erzhiban memorialized and impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Tangqishi's nephew Mamasha was commander of the Qipchaq personal army and acted lawlessly; Duo'erzhiban memorialized and impeached him.

sentences.zh: 马马沙因集无赖子欲加害，会唐其势被诛，乃罢。

translations.literal: Mamasha therefore gathered worthless fellows intending to do him harm, but as Tangqishi was executed, it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Mamasha gathered worthless fellows intending to harm him, but as Tangqishi was executed, the plot ceased.

sentences.zh: 迁太府监，改奎章阁学士院供奉学士，进承制学士，皆兼经筵官，又升侍书学士、同知经筵事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to superintendent of the Grand Storehouse, changed to supplying academician of the Hall of Splendid Letters, advanced to drafting academician—all concurrently Classics Colloquium officials—and was further promoted to academician attendant and associate director of Classics Colloquium affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to superintendent of the Grand Storehouse, made supplying academician of the Hall of Splendid Letters, advanced to drafting academician, all concurrently Classics Colloquium officials, then promoted to academician attendant and associate director of Classics Colloquium affairs.

sentences.zh: 是时朵尔直班甫弱冠，又世家子，乃独以经术侍帝左右，世以为盛事。

translations.literal: At that time Duo'erzhiban had just passed the weak-crown age and was moreover the son of a hereditary house, yet alone served the emperor at his side with classical learning—the age regarded it as a grand event.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Duo'erzhiban had just passed the weak-crown age and was the son of a hereditary house, yet alone served the emperor at his side with classical learning—the age regarded it as a grand event.

sentences.zh: 至正元年，罢学士院，除翰林学士，升资善大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizheng the Academy of Letters was abolished; he was removed to Hanlin academician and advanced to Grand Master for Cherishing the People.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizheng the Academy of Letters was abolished; he was made Hanlin academician and advanced to grand master for cherishing the people.

sentences.zh: 于是经筵亦归翰林，仍命朵尔直班知经筵事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Classics Colloquium also returned to the Hanlin, and Duo'erzhiban was still ordered to direct Classics Colloquium affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Classics Colloquium also returned to the Hanlin, and Duo'erzhiban was still ordered to direct its affairs.

sentences.zh: 是时康里巙巙以翰林学士承旨亦在经筵，在上前敷陈经义，朵尔直班则为翻译，曲尽其意，多所启沃，禁中语秘不传。

translations.literal: At that time Kangli Chuangchuang, as Hanlin academician and drafting academician, was also at the Classics Colloquium; before the emperor he expounded the classics' meaning, and Duo'erzhiban served as translator, fully conveying the intent and offering much counsel—palace speech was secret and not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kangli Chuangchuang, as Hanlin drafting academician, was also at the Classics Colloquium. Before the emperor he expounded the classics' meaning and Duo'erzhiban served as translator, fully conveying the intent and offering much counsel—palace speech was secret and not transmitted.

sentences.zh: 俄迁大宗正府也可扎鲁火赤，听讼之际，引谕律令，曲当事情。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be yeke jarquchi of the Grand Council for the Imperial Clan; when hearing lawsuits he cited and guided through the statutes and ordinances, fitting the circumstances of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to yeke jarquchi of the Grand Council for the Imperial Clan. When hearing lawsuits he cited the statutes and ordinances, fitting each circumstance.

sentences.zh: 有同僚年老者，叹曰：「吾居是官四十年，见公论事殆神人也。」

translations.literal: A colleague of advanced age sighed and said: "I have held this office forty years and have seen the gentleman discuss affairs—he is nearly divine."
translations.idiomatic: A colleague of advanced age sighed and said, "I have held this office forty years and have seen the gentleman discuss affairs—he is nearly divine."

sentences.zh: 宗王有杀其大母者，朵尔直班与同僚拔实力请于朝，必正其罪。

translations.literal: An imperial prince had killed his father's principal wife; Duo'erzhiban together with his colleague Bashi requested of the court that the crime must be rectified.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial prince had killed his father's principal wife. Duo'erzhiban together with his colleague Bashi requested of the court that the crime must be rectified.

sentences.zh: 时相难之。

translations.literal: The chief minister at the time made difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister at the time made difficulties.

sentences.zh: 出为淮东肃政廉访使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as surveillance commissioner of Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as surveillance commissioner of Huaidong.

sentences.zh: 迁江南行台治书侍御史，未行，又迁江西行省左丞，以疾不赴。

translations.literal: He was transferred to associate censor of the Secretariat of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat but did not go; he was again transferred to left vice councilor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat but did not take up the post because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to associate censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat but did not go; he was again transferred to left vice councilor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat but did not take up the post because of illness.

sentences.zh: 北还，养疾黄厓山中。

translations.literal: Returning north, he nursed his illness in the Huangya Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Returning north, he nursed his illness in the Huangya Mountains.

sentences.zh: 起为资正院使。

translations.literal: He was recalled to be superintendent of the Hall of Correct Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to be superintendent of the Hall of Correct Governance.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜中书参知政事、同知经筵事，提调宣文阁。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed associate administrative councilor of the Secretariat and associate director of Classics Colloquium affairs, and supervised the Hall of Promoting Culture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed associate administrative councilor of the Secretariat and associate director of Classics Colloquium affairs, and supervised the Hall of Promoting Culture.

sentences.zh: 时纂集《至正条格》，朵尔直班以谓是书上有祖宗制诰，安得独称今日年号；

translations.literal: At that time the 《Statutes of Zhizheng》 were being compiled; Duo'erzhiban said that this book contained above the regulatory edicts of the ancestors—how could one alone use today's reign title?
translations.idiomatic: At that time the 《Statutes of Zhizheng》 were being compiled. Duo'erzhiban said the book contained above the regulatory edicts of the ancestors—how could one alone use today's reign title?

sentences.zh: 又律中条格乃其一门耳，安可独以为书名。

translations.literal: Moreover, within the law the section on regulations is but one category—how could it alone serve as the book's title?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, within the law the section on regulations is but one category—how could it alone be the book's title?

sentences.zh: 时相不能从，唯除制诰而已。

translations.literal: The chief minister at the time could not follow him; only the regulatory edicts were removed.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister could not follow him; only the regulatory edicts were removed.

sentences.zh: 有以善音乐得幸者，有旨用为崇文监丞。

translations.literal: Someone skilled in music gained favor; there was an edict to use him as deputy superintendent of the Chongwen Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Someone skilled in music gained favor; there was an edict to appoint him deputy superintendent of the Chongwen Directorate.

sentences.zh: 朵尔直班它拟一人以闻。

translations.literal: Duo'erzhiban nominated another man and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhiban nominated another man and reported it.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「选法尽由中书省耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said in anger: "Is the selection law entirely in the hands of the Secretariat?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said angrily, "Is the selection law entirely in the hands of the Secretariat?"

sentences.zh: 朵尔直班顿首曰：「用幸人居清选，臣恐后世议陛下。

translations.literal: Duo'erzhiban bowed his head and said: "If a favorite is placed in a pure selection post, I fear later generations will criticize Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhiban bowed his head and said, "If a favorite is placed in a pure selection post, I fear later generations will criticize Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 今选它人，臣之罪也，省臣无与焉。」

translations.literal: If another is now selected, the fault is mine; the Secretariat ministers have no part in it."
translations.idiomatic: If another is now selected, the fault is mine; the secretariat ministers have no part in it."

sentences.zh: 帝乃悦。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon was pleased.

sentences.zh: 升右丞，寻拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right vice councilor and soon appointed vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice councilor and soon appointed vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 监察御史劾奏别兒怯不花，章甫上，黜御史大夫懿怜真班为江浙行省平章政事。

translations.literal: Investigating censors memorialized and impeached Bieqiebuha; when the memorial was submitted, Grand Censor Yilianzhenban was demoted to pacification commissioner of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censors memorialized and impeached Bieqiebuha. When the memorial was submitted, Grand Censor Yilianzhenban was demoted to pacification commissioner of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 朵尔直班曰：「若此则台纲安在？」

translations.literal: Duo'erzhiban said: "If it is like this, where is the censorate's great cord?"
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhiban said, "If it is like this, where is the censorate's great cord?"

sentences.zh: 乃再上章劾奏，并留大夫，不允。

translations.literal: He then again submitted a memorial impeaching and also requested to retain the grand censor, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He then again submitted a memorial impeaching and requested to retain the grand censor, but it was not granted.

sentences.zh: 台臣皆上印绶辞职。

translations.literal: The censorate officials all submitted their seals and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate officials all submitted their seals and resigned.

sentences.zh: 帝谕朵尔直班曰：「汝其毋辞。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed Duo'erzhiban: "You must not resign."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Duo'erzhiban, "You must not resign."

sentences.zh: 对曰：「宪纲隳矣，臣安得独留？」

translations.literal: He answered: "The great cord of the constitution has collapsed—how can I alone remain?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The great cord of the constitution has collapsed—how can I alone remain?"

sentences.zh: 帝为之出涕。

translations.literal: The emperor wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept for him.

sentences.zh: 朵尔直班即杜门谢宾客。

translations.literal: Duo'erzhiban at once shut his door and declined guests.
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhiban at once shut his door and declined guests.

sentences.zh: 寻出为辽阳行省平章政事，阶荣禄大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as pacification commissioner of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, with the rank of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as pacification commissioner of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, with the rank of grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 至官，询民所疾苦，知米粟羊豕薪炭诸货皆藉乡民贩负入城，而贵室僮奴、公府隶卒争强买之，仅酬其半直。

translations.literal: Upon reaching his post he inquired into the people's hardships and learned that rice, millet, sheep, pigs, fuel, and charcoal—all goods—depended on country people carrying them into the city, while the household slaves of noble houses and the runners of government offices contended to buy them by force, paying only half the fair price.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching his post he inquired into the people's hardships. Rice, millet, sheep, pigs, fuel, and charcoal all depended on country people carrying them into the city, while noble household slaves and government runners contended to buy by force, paying only half the fair price.

sentences.zh: 又其俗编柳为斗，大小不一，豪贾猾侩得以高下其手，民咸病之。

translations.literal: Moreover, by custom they wove willow into pecks of uneven size, so that powerful merchants and crafty brokers could raise or lower them at will, and the people all suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they wove willow into pecks of uneven size, so powerful merchants and crafty brokers could manipulate them at will and the people all suffered.

sentences.zh: 即饬有司厉防禁，齐称量，诸物乃毕集而价自平。

translations.literal: He at once ordered the relevant offices to enforce strict prohibitions and standardize weights and measures; all goods then gathered completely and prices of themselves became fair.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the relevant offices to enforce strict prohibitions and standardize weights and measures; all goods then gathered and prices of themselves became fair.

sentences.zh: 又存恤孤老，平准钱法，清铨选，汰胥吏，慎勾稽，兴废坠，巨细毕举。

translations.literal: He also cared for orphans and the aged, stabilized the money law, cleared selections, cut redundant clerks, was careful in audit, and revived what had fallen—great and small were all accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: He also cared for orphans and the aged, stabilized the money law, cleared selections, cut redundant clerks, was careful in audit, and revived what had fallen—great and small were all accomplished.

sentences.zh: 苟有罪，虽勋旧不贷。

translations.literal: If there was guilt, even meritorious old families were not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: If there was guilt, even meritorious old families were not pardoned.

sentences.zh: 王邸百司闻风悚惧。

translations.literal: The hundred offices of princely establishments heard the wind and were fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred offices of princely establishments heard the wind and were fearful.

sentences.zh: 召为太常礼仪院使，俄迁中政使，又迁资正使。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be superintendent of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; soon transferred to superintendent of the Central Administration, then again superintendent of the Hall of Correct Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to superintendent of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, soon transferred to superintendent of the Central Administration, then again superintendent of the Hall of Correct Governance.

sentences.zh: 会盗起河南，帝忧之。

translations.literal: When bandits arose in Henan, the emperor was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits arose in Henan, the emperor was troubled.

sentences.zh: 拜中书平章政事，阶光禄大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed pacification commissioner of the Secretariat, with the rank of Grand Master for Splendid Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed pacification commissioner of the Secretariat, with the rank of grand master for splendid brightness.

sentences.zh: 首言：「治国之道，纲常为重。

translations.literal: He first said: "In governing the state, the great constants are what weigh most heavily.
translations.idiomatic: He first said, "In governing the state, the great constants weigh most heavily.

sentences.zh: 前西台御史张桓伏节死义，不污于寇，宜首旌之，以劝来者。」

translations.literal: The former Western Branch Secretariat censor Zhang Huan upheld integrity and died for righteousness, unstained by the bandits—he ought first to be honored to encourage those who come after."
translations.idiomatic: The former Western Branch censor Zhang Huan upheld integrity and died for righteousness, unstained by the bandits—he ought first to be honored to encourage those who come after."

sentences.zh: 又言：「宜守荆襄、湖广以绝后患。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Jingxiang and Huguang ought to be held to cut off later troubles."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Jingxiang and Huguang ought to be held to cut off later troubles."

sentences.zh: 又数论：「祖宗之用兵，匪专于杀人，盖必有其道焉。

translations.literal: He repeatedly discussed: "When the ancestors used troops, it was not solely to kill people—there must certainly have been a Way in it.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly discussed, "When the ancestors used troops it was not solely to kill people—there must have been a Way in it.

sentences.zh: 今倡乱者止数人，顾乃尽坐中华之民为畔逆，岂足以服人心。」

translations.literal: Today those who stir disorder are only a few men, yet all the people of the Central Plains are treated as rebels—how can that suffice to win people's hearts?"
translations.idiomatic: Today those who stir disorder are only a few men, yet all the people of the Central Plains are treated as rebels—how can that win people's hearts?"

sentences.zh: 其言颇迕丞相脱脱意。

translations.literal: His words largely ran counter to Chief Councilor Toghto's intent.
translations.idiomatic: His words largely ran counter to Chief Councilor Toghto's intent.

sentences.zh: 时脱脱倚信左司郎中汝中柏、员外郎伯帖木兒，故两人因擅权用事，而朵尔直班正色立朝，无所附丽。

translations.literal: At the time Toghto relied on Left Secretariat Director Ru Zhongbai and section director Botiemuer; therefore the two men usurped power and handled affairs, while Duo'erzhiban stood upright at court and attached himself to no faction.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Toghto relied on Left Secretariat Director Ru Zhongbai and section director Botiemuer, so the two usurped power, while Duo'erzhiban stood upright at court and attached himself to no faction.

sentences.zh: 适陕州危急，因出为陕西行台御史大夫。

translations.literal: As Shaanzhou was critically pressed, he was therefore sent out as grand censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: As Shaanzhou was critically pressed, he was sent out as grand censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 行至中途，闻商州陷，武关不守，即轻骑昼夜兼程至奉元，而贼已至鸿门。

translations.literal: When he reached the midway point he heard that Shangzhou had fallen and Wuguan was not held; he at once took light horsemen and pressed day and night to Fengyuan, while the bandits had already reached Hongmen.
translations.idiomatic: Midway he heard Shangzhou had fallen and Wuguan was lost. He took light horsemen and pressed day and night to Fengyuan while the bandits had already reached Hongmen.

sentences.zh: 吏白涓日署事，不许，曰：「贼势若此，尚何顾阴阳拘忌哉！」

translations.literal: The clerks reported that he should take office on an auspicious day; he would not permit it and said: "The bandits' power is like this—how can one still care for yin-yang taboos!"
translations.idiomatic: The clerks said he should take office on an auspicious day; he refused and said, "The bandits' power is like this—how can one still care for yin-yang taboos!"

sentences.zh: 即就署。

translations.literal: He at once assumed office.
translations.idiomatic: He at once assumed office.

sentences.zh: 省、台素以举措为嫌，不相聚论事。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat and the Branch Censorate, by custom regarding each other's measures with suspicion, did not gather to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat and branch censorate, by custom suspicious of each other's measures, did not gather to discuss affairs.

sentences.zh: 朵尔直班曰：「多事如此，恶得以常例论？」

translations.literal: Duo'erzhiban said: "With so many affairs, how can one discuss by regular precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhiban said, "With so many affairs, how can one discuss by regular precedent?"

sentences.zh: 乃与行省平章朵朵约五日一会集。

translations.literal: He then agreed with Pacification Commissioner Duoduo to meet every five days.
translations.idiomatic: He then agreed with Pacification Commissioner Duoduo to meet every five days.

sentences.zh: 寻有旨，命与朵朵便宜同讨贼，即督诸军复商州。

translations.literal: Soon there was an edict ordering him and Duoduo, as circumstances required, jointly to suppress the bandits; he at once supervised the armies and recovered Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered him and Duoduo, as circumstances required, jointly to suppress the bandits. He supervised the armies and recovered Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 乃修筑奉元城垒。

translations.literal: He then repaired the ramparts of Fengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then repaired the ramparts of Fengyuan.

sentences.zh: 募民为兵，出库所藏银为大钱，射而中的者赏之，由是人皆为精兵。

translations.literal: He recruited the people as soldiers, took silver stored in the treasury to make large coins, and rewarded those who hit the target in archery; thereby everyone became picked troops.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited the people as soldiers, took silver from the treasury to make large coins, and rewarded those who hit the target in archery; thereby everyone became picked troops.

sentences.zh: 金、商义兵以兽皮为矢房，状如瓠，号毛葫芦军，甚精锐，列其功以闻，赐敕书褒奖之，由是其军遂盛，而国家获其用。

translations.literal: The righteous armies of Jin and Shang used animal hides for arrow quivers shaped like gourds, called the Maohulu Army, very picked and sharp; their achievements were listed and reported, and an edict of commendation was granted to praise them—thereby that army grew strong and the state obtained its use.
translations.idiomatic: The righteous armies of Jin and Shang used animal hides for arrow quivers shaped like gourds, called the Maohulu Army, very picked and sharp. Their achievements were reported and an edict of commendation granted; thereby that army grew strong and the state obtained its use.

sentences.zh: 金州由兴元、凤翔达奉元，道里回远，乃开义谷，创置七驿，路近以便。

translations.literal: Jin Prefecture reached Fengyuan by way of Xingyuan and Fengxiang over a long roundabout route; he therefore opened the Righteous Valley and newly established seven post stations, making the road shorter and convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Prefecture reached Fengyuan by way of Xingyuan and Fengxiang over a long roundabout route. He opened the Righteous Valley and established seven post stations, making the road shorter and convenient.

sentences.zh: 时御史大夫也先帖木兒师败于河南，西台御史蒙古鲁海牙、范文等十二人劾奏之。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Censor Yexiantiemuer's army was defeated in Henan; Western Branch censors Mongoluhaiya, Fan Wen, and twelve others memorialized and impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Grand Censor Yexiantiemuer's army was defeated in Henan. Western Branch censors Mongoluhaiya, Fan Wen, and twelve others memorialized and impeached him.

sentences.zh: 朵尔直班当署字，顾谓左右曰：「吾其为平章湖广矣。」

translations.literal: Duo'erzhiban was to countersign; he turned and said to those at hand: "I shall become pacification commissioner of Huguang."
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhiban was to countersign. He turned and said to those at hand, "I shall become pacification commissioner of Huguang."

sentences.zh: 未几命下，果然。

translations.literal: Before long the order came down, and it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the order came down, and it was indeed so.

sentences.zh: 也先帖木兒者，脱脱之弟，章既上，脱脱怒，故左迁朵尔直班，而御史十二人皆见黜。

translations.literal: Yexiantiemuer was Toghto's younger brother; once the memorial was submitted Toghto was angry, and therefore Duo'erzhiban was demoted to the left, while the twelve censors were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yexiantiemuer was Toghto's younger brother. Once the memorial was submitted Toghto was angry, Duo'erzhiban was demoted, and all twelve censors were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 关中人遮道涕泣曰：「生我者公也，何遽去我而不留乎？」

translations.literal: The people within the passes blocked the road weeping and saying: "You gave us life—why do you suddenly leave us and not stay?"
translations.idiomatic: The people within the passes blocked the road weeping and saying, "You gave us life—why do you suddenly leave us and not stay?"

sentences.zh: 朵尔直班慰遣之，不听，乃从间道得出。

translations.literal: Duo'erzhiban comforted and sent them off, but they would not listen; he therefore got out by a bypath.
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhiban comforted and sent them off, but they would not listen; he therefore got out by a bypath.

sentences.zh: 至重庆，闻江陵陷，道路阻不可行，或请少留以俟之，不从，期必达乃已。

translations.literal: When he reached Chongqing he heard that Jiangling had fallen and the roads were blocked and impassable. Some asked him to stay awhile and wait, but he would not follow them and fixed on reaching his destination as his limit.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Chongqing he heard Jiangling had fallen and the roads were blocked. Some asked him to stay awhile, but he would not and fixed on reaching his destination.

sentences.zh: 湖广行省时权治澧州，既至，律诸军以法，而授纳粟者以官，人心翕然。

translations.literal: The Huguang Branch Secretariat at the time governed provisionally from Li Prefecture. Once he arrived he regulated the armies by law and granted office to those who submitted grain; the people's hearts were united.
translations.idiomatic: The Huguang Branch Secretariat governed provisionally from Li Prefecture. Once he arrived he regulated the armies by law and granted office to those who submitted grain; the people's hearts were united.

sentences.zh: 汝中柏、伯帖木兒言于丞相曰：「不杀朵尔直班，则丞相终不安。」

translations.literal: Ru Zhongbai and Botiemuer spoke to the chief councilor, saying: "If Duo'erzhiban is not killed, the chief councilor will never be secure."
translations.idiomatic: Ru Zhongbai and Botiemuer told the chief councilor, "If Duo'erzhiban is not killed, the chief councilor will never be secure."

sentences.zh: 盖谓其帝意所眷属，必复用耳。

translations.literal: This meant that because the emperor favored him, he would certainly be used again.
translations.idiomatic: They meant that because the emperor favored him, he would certainly be used again.

sentences.zh: 乃命朵尔直班职专供给军食。

translations.literal: He was therefore ordered that Duo'erzhiban's duty should be solely to supply army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore ordered that Duo'erzhiban's duty should be solely to supply army provisions.

sentences.zh: 时官廪所储无几，即延州民有粟者，亲予酒谕劝之而贷其粟，约俟朝廷颁钞至即还以直，民无不从者。

translations.literal: At the time what the government granaries stored was scant. He at once summoned state people who had grain, personally gave them wine to advise and encourage them, and borrowed their grain, agreeing that when the court issued notes they would immediately be repaid at full value—the people none failed to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Government granaries held little. He summoned state people who had grain, personally gave them wine to encourage them, and borrowed their grain, agreeing that when the court issued notes they would be repaid at full value—the people all complied.

sentences.zh: 又遣官籴粟河南、四川之境，民闻其名，争输粟以助军饷。

translations.literal: He also sent officials to purchase grain in the borders of Henan and Sichuan; hearing his name, the people vied to submit grain to aid army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent officials to purchase grain in Henan and Sichuan. Hearing his name, the people vied to submit grain to aid army provisions.

sentences.zh: 右丞伯颜不花方总兵，承顺风旨，数侵辱之。

translations.literal: Right Vice Councilor Bayanbuhua was then commanding troops and, following the prevailing wind of court favor, repeatedly insulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Councilor Bayanbuhua was commanding troops and, following the prevailing court favor, repeatedly insulted him.

sentences.zh: 朵尔直班不为动。

translations.literal: Duo'erzhiban was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Duo'erzhiban was unmoved.

sentences.zh: 会官军复武昌，至蕲、黄伯颜不花百计征索，无不给之，犹欲言其供需失期。

translations.literal: When the government army recovered Wuchang and reached Qi and Huang, Bayanbuhua sought supplies by a hundred schemes and was given everything, yet still wished to say that provisions were delivered late.
translations.idiomatic: When the government army recovered Wuchang and reached Qi and Huang, Bayanbuhua sought supplies by a hundred schemes and was given everything, yet still wished to say provisions were delivered late.

sentences.zh: 达剌罕军帅王不花奋言曰：「平章国之贵臣，今坐不重茵，食无珍味，徒为我曹军食耳。

translations.literal: The darqan army commander Wangbuhua spoke forcefully: "The pacification commissioner is the state's honored minister; today he sits without a heavy mat and eats without fine flavors, serving only as provisions for us soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The darqan army commander Wangbuhua spoke forcefully, "The pacification commissioner is the state's honored minister. Today he sits without a heavy mat and eats without fine flavors, serving only as provisions for us soldiers.

sentences.zh: 今百需立办，顾犹欲诬之，是无人心也。

translations.literal: Now a hundred needs are furnished at once, yet you still wish to slander him—there is no human heart in this.
translations.idiomatic: Now a hundred needs are furnished at once, yet you still wish to slander him—there is no human heart in this.

sentences.zh: 我曹便当散还乡里矣。」

translations.literal: We ought at once to disperse and return to our home districts."
translations.idiomatic: We ought at once to disperse and return to our home districts."

sentences.zh: 脱脱遣国子助教完者至军中，风使害之。

translations.literal: Toghto sent the National University lecturer Wanzhe to the army with a wind to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Toghto sent the National University lecturer Wanzhe to the army with instructions to harm him.

sentences.zh: 完者至，则反加敬礼，语人曰：「平章勋旧之家，国之祥瑞，吾苟伤之，则人将不食吾余矣。」

translations.literal: When Wanzhe arrived he instead showed added respect and said to people: "The pacification commissioner is of a meritorious old house—the state's auspicious omen. If I should harm him, people will not eat my leftovers."
translations.idiomatic: When Wanzhe arrived he instead showed added respect and said, "The pacification commissioner is of a meritorious old house—the state's auspicious omen. If I should harm him, people will not eat my leftovers."

sentences.zh: 朵尔直班素有风疾，军中感雾露，所患日剧，遂卒于黄州兰溪驿，年四十。

translations.literal: Duo'erzhiban had long had wind illness; in the army, affected by mist and dew, his ailment grew daily worse, and he therefore died at the Lanxi post station in Huang Prefecture at the age of forty.
